representation: Frozen final-token hidden state, batch-of-four extraction, and a numeric logistic head
training_sources: Apache-2.0 Cisco Outshift TBAC generated pre-call dialogue validation
decision: Rejected: dialogue ranking improved over frozen transfer, but single-turn tool relevance regressed and false allowances remain on every transfer domain at the cautious threshold. Nothing is loaded by Heliox.
failure_analysis: High-scoring errors include semantically adjacent but wrong MCP tools, cross-tenant action scope, changing a document when chat-only output was requested, and broadening a single-device alarm to all paired devices. The frozen representation does not reliably model tool identity, target, or output-boundary constraints.
limitations: Official test partitions were outside fitting and calibration, but prior results on those same tests guided this experiment; this is adaptive research, not a blind benchmark. Generated dialogue relevance is not authorization. The Heliox suite is synthetic and previously inspected. Batch extraction differs numerically from one-by-one extraction, so this report uses a separate consistently batched feature set. No result establishes Jev parity or live desktop safety.
